name: Auto Chapters
description: Finds where programmes with no chapter markers fade to black (and go quiet), and uses those moments for mid-roll breaks instead of cutting at a fixed interval. Programmes are analysed in the background with ffmpeg, those about to air first.
author: SchedularrTV
lowPowerNotice: each analysis decodes a whole programme, which takes minutes per episode here (more for HEVC or 4K) and competes with the channels on air. Keep one at a time, leave the whole-library scan off, and let it use the hardware decoder.

settings.label: Use the markers found for mid-roll breaks
settings.description: Programmes with chapter markers of their own keep them. Turn this off to analyse programmes without changing where breaks go yet.

settings.label: Only count fades to black where the sound drops out too
settings.description: Real ad-break points fade picture and sound together; dark scenes with dialogue don't. Turn off for programmes whose breaks keep music playing.

settings.label: Shortest fade to black (seconds)
settings.description: Black shorter than this is ignored (camera flashes, quick cuts).

settings.label: How dark counts as black (0 to 1)
settings.description: Raise it for programmes whose fades only reach dark grey; lower it if dark scenes are mistaken for breaks.

settings.label: Analyse the whole library in the background
settings.description: Off: only programmes in the schedule are analysed, as they come up. On: every episode and movie without chapters is, which can take a long time for a big library.
settings.lowPowerNote: Leave this off here: a whole library can mean days of full CPU.

settings.label: Programmes analysed at once
settings.description: Each decodes a whole video, so more than 1 or 2 slows everything else on this computer.

settings.label: Decoder threads
settings.description: Processor threads each analysis may use. Fewer is slower but leaves the rest for the channels on air. Leave empty for the default.

settings.label: Hardware decoding
settings.description: Let the graphics or video chip decode instead of the processor (ffmpeg's -hwaccel). auto picks one if there is one; drm is the Raspberry Pi's. A file it can't decode is read in software instead. Leave empty for the default: off, or auto on a Raspberry Pi.
settings.lowPowerNote: auto (the default here) lets the Pi's chip decode HEVC, much faster than the processor.

settings.label: ffmpeg
settings.description: Leave empty to use the ffmpeg set under App settings.
